audits.what_it_does: `discover_entries` finds 44 payloads (12 skills x 2 planes, 7 Claude agents, 5 commands, 7 Codex agents, 1 workflow) and places each under `~/.claude/{skills,agents,commands,workflows}` or `$CODEX_HOME`. Default mode is `auto`, which on Unix means 44 symlinks into the checkout; `--copy` and the Windows fallback copy trees instead. Ownership lives in one JSON document under XDG_STATE_HOME, and every entry carries a content digest plus a `stat-v2:<dev>:<ino>:<btime>` physical-identity witness for itself, its collection directory, and its configured root. On top of that sit five more layers: (1) per-entry crash-consistent transactions — stage into a private 0700 container, journal an `armed` record, publish with `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` / `renameatx_np` / Win32 `FILE_RENAME_INFORMATION_EX`, retire the container, journal `resolved`; (2) a `classify_recovery` state machine enumerating ~25 (operation, phase, live, staged, backup) tuples that a later run replays to finish or roll back an interrupted command; (3) durability barriers — `fsync_tree` over every file of every payload, `fsync_directory` on each parent, `F_FULLFSYNC` on Darwin; (4) a birth-quantum `SettlementLedger` that probes whether a recorded btime can be distinguished from a later replacement's, marks records `witness_settled: false` when it cannot, and pays one bounded 3s wait per command; (5) v1→v2→v3 state migration plus a four-phase crash-consistent rename protocol whose entire input is the private map `{"agentic-sdlc-orchestrator": "agentic-sdlc"}`. `install_operator_tools.py` does the parallel job for two files (`ccodex`, `agentic-sdlc-statusline`) and is the control group: same conflict/adopt/refresh/uninstall semantics, `{path, digest, removable}` records, `mkstemp`+`fsync`+`os.replace`, one `pending` slot — and no identity witness, no settlement, no NOREPLACE, no phase machine.
audits.replacement: Keep the operator surface and the atomicity; delete the physical-identity and journal layers. Concretely, keep as-is: `discover_entries`, `destination_for`, `assert_safe_collection` (a real boundary — it refuses when `~/.claude/skills` is itself a symlink or the destination escapes the configured root), `digest`/`tree_manifest`/`content_equivalent` (this IS the manifest), the link/copy/junction primitives, `marketplace_overlap`, `installer_lock`, `_install`/`status`/`uninstall`/CLI, and `readonly_projection` (`ccodex sdlc doctor` consumes it at scripts/ccodex_sdlc.py:1554). Replace the rest with the shape install_operator_tools.py already ships: records become `{agent, kind, name, source, mode, digest, removable}`; `entry_matches_record` becomes mode + link-target + `digest(destination) == record["digest"]` (~30 lines, no `stat_identity`); publication becomes stage into a sibling `.<name>.tmp` then `os.replace` into place (~40 lines — atomic for a symlink in two calls, and for a copy-mode tree via rename-aside-then-replace); state persistence becomes `atomic_write` + `sync_directory` lifted verbatim from install_operator_tools.py:446-467 (~40 lines, dropping `fsync_tree`); ordering becomes manifest-entry-first-then-publish, so a crash leaves a recorded path that does not exist — which `status` already reports `absent` and `install` already writes. Then delete: the statx/Win32 ctypes structs (48), the identity + witness + `SettlementLedger` block (484, lines 342-825), `_rename_noreplace` and its three platform bodies (244, lines 2308-2551), the private-artifact/staging/transaction-record block (268, net 228), `classify_recovery` + `execute_recovery` + `recover_transactions` (424), `transactional_create/replace/delete/rename` (316, net 256), and the v1-migration + one-skill rename-migration block (379 — there are zero published releases and zero version tags, so every ownership document in existence is on the author's own machines and `rm state.json && reinstall` fixes it). Two facts make this a substitution rather than a bet: install_operator_tools.py is the same design already shipping and tested in this repo, and `test_replaced_tree_is_refused_under_a_coarse_birth_clock` (tests/test_install_skill_bundle.py:2682) states the witness's entire marginal value in its own comment — "The replacement is byte-identical, so the recorded digest still matches and only the physical witness can refuse it."
audits.risk_if_deleted: The one real loss is atomic publication, and the replacement keeps it, so name the residuals instead. (1) In `--copy`/Windows mode only, a crash during a refresh — Ctrl-C, or the WSL2 OOM kill this repo's own memory records — between the rename-aside and the replace leaves the old tree orphaned at `~/.claude/skills/.agentic-sdlc.old` (58 files, 3.4MB) and nothing at `agentic-sdlc`. The operator sees a missing skill, `status` says `absent`, re-running install restores it, and they must hand-delete the `.old` leftover from a printed message. Today `classify_recovery` repairs that automatically. (2) `uninstall` will remove a destination the operator replaced with byte-identical content, where today it refuses with `conflict:` and preserves. That is not a loss: byte-identical means the bytes present are the bundle's own, and any content the operator actually added changes the tree digest, which `entry_matches_record` already catches without any btime. (3) `ccodex sdlc recover --apply` loses its subject and goes with it. What the deletion buys back cuts the same way and is the sharper fact: `stat_identity` raises `filesystem does not expose stable object identity` whenever statx does not mask STATX_BTIME, and `_rename_noreplace` raises `atomic no-replace rename requires glibc 2.28 or newer` when the symbol is absent — so today an operator whose `$HOME` is on NFS, or on a FUSE/overlay mount that reports no birth time, or on musl before it exported renameat2, cannot install 4,309 lines of markdown at all, on a host where `cp -r` works. And the layer causing that refusal has never answered an operator report: commit 374eec6 sources it entirely to a CI runner's coarse birth clock ("On the CI runner's filesystem the advisory probe measured...", CI run 32554149554), i.e. it was added so a probe this repo wrote about its own witness scheme would stop failing. The subsystem itself is load-bearing — delete it outright and nothing installs, and scripts/ccodex_sdlc_install.py:1782 loads it as a sibling and reuses `transactional_create`, `transactional_replace`, `installer_lock`, and `entry_matches_record`, so ADR-0021's ccodex path needs a surviving core. That is why this is shrink-hard and not delete: keep ~1,530 lines that place 44 symlinks and refuse to clobber, and drop the 2,330 that defend a race the module's own docstring already declares out of scope ("A same-UID racer ... is out of scope").

audits.subsystem: Release-candidate acquisition engine — scripts/release_candidate.py (2,916), scripts/release_candidate_acquisition.py (3,535), tests/test_release_candidate.py (1,440), tests/test_release_candidate_acquisition.py (4,351), plus 707 lines of validator in scripts/validate_bundle.py and policy/release-candidate{,-acquisition,-execution}.v1.json
audits.what_it_does: Two Python entrypoints that build, verify, and durably install a self-built tarball of this repository. `release_candidate.py build` reads the committed git tree (refusing dirty or ambiguous source), copies an allowlisted payload subset plus a relocatable uv-managed CPython 3.12.11 into a staging tree, writes a canonical `manifest.json` carrying a per-entry digest inventory, and emits a deterministic ustar/gzip `agentic-sdlc-candidate-<sha256>-linux-x64.tar.gz` (uid/gid 0, empty uname/gname, mtime pinned to the commit epoch, fixed modes) via fsync + renameat2-NOREPLACE. `verify` re-opens that archive by descriptor, pre-flights raw ustar headers before letting `tarfile` touch it, extracts through openat-chained fds, and re-derives every digest without ever executing archive code. `run-readonly` extracts to a private 0700 temp dir and runs a closed four-command `ccodex sdlc` read-only grammar through the archive's own bundled Python under a supervised process group with a retained "effect-state" witness file. `release_candidate_acquisition.py` then adds a durable XDG install lifecycle: `acquire plan` seals a plan record over the archive/trust-root/XDG prestate digests; `acquire apply` demands an operator-hand-authored expiring single-use 19-field "procedural grant" bound to those digests, takes one writer lock, appends a hash-chained six-phase journal (opened→pinned→staged→published→receipted→installed-unselected) before any data effect, stages and publishes the tree no-replace, and seals an immutable receipt; `acquire recover inspect|finish` classifies a crash at any phase and finish-only advances it. Every record declares `public_channel: null`, `release_claim: "none"`, `support: "unsupported"`, `provenance: "unverified"`, `sbom: "absent"`, `purpose: "developer-only"`.
audits.replacement:
Keep a builder, delete the lifecycle. Five concrete pieces, ~190 lines total.

(1) `scripts/build_release.py`, ~120 lines: `git archive` the existing `policy/release-candidate.v1.json` payload allowlist into `dist/agentic-sdlc-<version>.tar.gz`, keep the `manifest.json` inventory, write `dist/SHA256SUMS`. `git archive` supplies the reproducible-build determinism for free (fixed mtime from the commit, uid/gid 0) — this is the one property in the 6,451 lines worth preserving, and it is a one-line risk if the replacement reaches for `tar czf` instead. DROP the bundled CPython: `mise.toml`'s existing pinned `[tools]` uv already supplies Python 3.12.11 to every entrypoint, and the interpreter is what forced the 128 MiB archive ceiling, the relocatability scan, the license-path check, and the staging runtime canary.

(2) A ~30-line GitHub Actions release job: on tag, run `mise run check`, run the builder, `gh release create` with the tarball and `SHA256SUMS`.

(3) Acquisition becomes `mise use -g github:Codeseys-Labs/agentic-sdlc@<version>`, or an `http:` entry pinned in the already-checked-in `mise.lock`. ZERO repo lines. `mise backends ls` — recorded in this repo's own `docs/research/2026-08-07-clone-free-install.md` — lists `github`, `http`, and `ubi`; mise owns version resolution, download, checksum verification, side-by-side versioned install dirs, and downgrade-by-version. Digest pinning is not lost by deleting this engine: it moves into the same `mise.lock` the project already reviews for its 12 other tools, which is exactly what ADR-0002 says mise is for.

(4) `scripts/write_acquisition_receipt.py`, ~40 lines, emitting the same sealed `release-candidate-acquisition-receipt/v1` JSON (sha256 over canonical bytes minus `record_sha256`) pointing at the mise-resolved root. This is NOT optional garnish — it must land in the same change, because it is the only thing keeping `ccodex sdlc install/update` alive. When that subsystem is next touched, replace its `admit_acquisition_receipt` with "read `manifest.json` at the mise-resolved root" and the receipt shape can go too; those are its lines, not this subsystem's.

(5) Keep `policy/release-candidate.v1.json` (payload allowlist + the honesty disclosures `public_channel`/`release_claim`/`support`) and its 140 validator lines. Cheap, and they are what stops this repo claiming a release it has not cut. `policy/release-contract.v1.json` and `test_release_contract.py` are a separate small subsystem — leave them alone.

DELETE OUTRIGHT: all of `release_candidate_acquisition.py` and its 4,351-line test file; the `run-readonly` bridge (~870 lines in `release_candidate.py`: `_validated_system_tmp`, `_retain_process_group_witness`, `_render_candidate_dispatcher`, `_admission_record`, `_converge_process_group`, `_supervise_candidate`, the v2 report validators, `run_readonly`) which has ZERO callers anywhere in the repo outside its own tests; the fd-custody verify path; and 567 validator lines (`validate_release_candidate_acquisition_policy` 329, `validate_release_candidate_acquisition_record` 185, `validate_release_candidate_execution_policy` 53).

WHY NOT "keep": three independent reasons. (a) The payload IS the machinery. The allowlist ships `scripts/` (34,602 lines), all of `skills/` (50,321, of which only 8,994 is markdown), `policy/`, `assets/`, `plugin/` — ~90,700 lines plus a full CPython, ceilings at 128 MiB compressed / 274 MB uncompressed — so that the installer can install 4,309 lines of markdown. (b) It reimplements mise for one artifact, beside a tool the project has already decided owns version resolution. (c) It defends a threat model the product disclaims in writing: `grant.approval_authenticated: false`, `grant.minted_by_tool: false`, `same_user: true`; `scripts/ccodex_sdlc_install.py:108-114` says the seal "is not a boundary against a same-UID forger"; AGENTS.md:407 says "Concurrent external mutation of managed paths during a write command is unsupported". The fd rechecks, dev/ino/btime prestate digests, writer lock, hash-chained journal and process-group witnesses all guard a same-UID racer that is explicitly out of scope — and they do not hold anyway. `docs/research/2026-08-22-ci-red-forensics.md:78-95` documents that `_pin_archive`'s substitution witness structurally cannot see the attack its own test asserts, passing locally only because a ctime was measured going backwards; open Seeds bugs `agentic-sdlc-ba1a` (apply seals a receipt it never reads back) and `agentic-sdlc-db15` (RootPin persists a birth-timestamp prestate that cannot distinguish a same-quantum replacement) are two more of the same class, both labeled trust-boundary, both still open. This machinery is generating its own defect stream against an adversary it has declared unsupported.

WHY NOT "delete": the receipt+root contract has two live consumers (4,590 lines), and `build`'s deterministic digest-named tarball is precisely what the vision needs. Note also that `install` does not trust this engine's verification — it independently re-derives the receipt seal (`acquisition_record_digest`), re-reads the candidate manifest, and re-verifies every entry it copies against the manifest inventory (`ccodex_sdlc_install.py:111-113`). Everything the 6,451 lines proves at extraction time is proven again at activation time.
audits.risk_if_deleted:
The failure that actually happens: an operator types `ccodex sdlc install --host claude` on a machine where `acquire apply` was never run and gets `no acquired candidate is available: the acquisition receipts directory <path> is absent or is not an exact directory. Acquire a candidate first; this operation never acquires one` (scripts/ccodex_sdlc_install.py:636-638) — a refusal naming a command that no longer exists and that no README, AGENTS.md, or mise task ever described. That turns 4,590 lines (`ccodex_sdlc_install.py` 2,004 + `ccodex_sdlc_update.py` 2,586) into dead entry points reachable from the shipped launcher's own help text (`assets/launchers/ccodex.in:137-140`). This is why the ~40-line receipt shim is a prerequisite of the deletion, not a follow-up.

Second, smaller and real: anyone who has already run `acquire apply` on this host holds an XDG plane at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/agentic-sdlc/acquisition/` and `$XDG_STATE_HOME/agentic-sdlc/acquisition/` that nothing can afterward inspect, finish, or recover — `acquire recover` is the ONLY reader of those journals anywhere in the repo (verified: grep finds the engine and the validator's schema table, no other consumer). A crash that left a journal at `staged` or `published` strands a partially published candidate tree with no tool that can classify it. Mitigation is one paragraph in the deletion commit saying `rm -rf` both directories, which is safe precisely because the terminal state is `installed-unselected` and nothing is ever activated from it — but omit that paragraph and the operator is left with a candidate root they cannot reason about.

Third: reproducibility, if the replacement builder is careless. `_write_ustar_archive`/`_tar_info` (release_candidate.py:1162-1241) pin uid/gid 0, empty uname/gname, mtime to the commit epoch, fixed modes, and a fixed gzip header, so two builds of one commit are byte-identical and the digest in the filename genuinely means "this commit". `git archive` preserves that; `tar czf` over a working tree does not, and the digest silently stops meaning anything.

What an operator would NOT notice, at all: every TOCTOU recheck, every prestate digest, the writer lock, the hash-chained journal, the six-phase crash taxonomy, the exit-4 witness records, the process-group converge/witness path, and the entire `run-readonly` bridge (zero callers). The journal exists to recover a crash mid-copy of a directory that can simply be re-copied from an immutable digest-named tarball — the recovery for "the install crashed" is "run it again", which the engine's own state machine already classifies as `success-no-effect`.

audits.what_it_does: Six standalone Python CLIs implement a closed JSON-document protocol for one "wave" of agentic work. `wave-plan-compiler` seals a WavePlan + PlanDiff from a mission contract and a planning snapshot; `wave-plan-admission` re-checks that sealed plan against a caller-supplied fresh snapshot and emits an admission report; `wave-submission` seals four kinds of worker submission (artifact manifest, review, critic findings, conductor record) with digests; `wave-journal` appends hash-chained JSONL lines (one per node disposition, budget, retry, approval) with a prev_digest chain, a 5-value exit contract, and an effect-admission ledger, and projects them without ever publishing a `complete` field; `wave-verdict` then derives exactly one of six terminal states from eight conditions across those documents plus the gate receipt; `sdlc-observability-projection` merges up to thirteen of these documents into one read-only status blob. Eleven schemas, no writes to any queue, no ability to stop a dispatch — every one of them is an optional post-hoc self-audit that the agent being audited chooses whether to invoke.
audits.replacement:
Two things, both already in the repo.

(1) `docs/evidence/waves/<wave-id>.md` — one hand-written markdown file per wave, ~30 lines: a table of `node | role | model_id | disposition | commit | reviewed-by`, one blockquote of the operator's verbatim approval with the date, the integration commit SHA, and the `self_digest` of the gate receipt from the merged head. The one real wave's 28 files / 462 lines of JSON compress to roughly 25 lines of this with no fact lost that anyone read.

(2) Four lines appended to `commands/sdlc-wave.md` step 8, each answered by something that already exists and is already trusted:
- `git log --format='%H %s' <base>..<branch>` — what the node actually did
- `git show --stat <integration-commit>` — the declared outputs really landed (this is verdict condition 3, for free, and unlike condition 3 it is anchored to a commit)
- the existing `scripts/gate_receipt.py` receipt on the merged head — condition 6, already self-hashing, already outside this subsystem
- reviewer ≠ implementer, and the approval blockquote's date precedes the integration commit's committer date — conditions 4 and 5, as a two-line reading, checkable by eye

Git already provides content-addressed, ordered, tamper-evident, authored history. This subsystem rebuilt a strictly weaker version of it in JSON alongside it: nothing locks, concurrency is "unsupported", the chain is "detection, not prevention", it is explicitly not safe against "a same-UID TOCTOU racer" — and `wave-verdict.py:340`'s own RESIDUALS concede the fatal gap, that condition 3 "hashes declared artifacts in the target tree as it is now; no Git snapshot, commit, or merge-base is verified" and that "freshness is underivable: a stale but internally consistent artifact set derives its state by construction." The 12,209 lines cannot answer whether the evidence is about the code that is there now. `git show --stat` answers it in one command.

Optional, if the operator wants the derivation mechanized rather than read: ~120 lines that parse the markdown table, read the gate receipt's outcome, and print accepted/blocked with named reasons. That is the whole of what condition 4, 5 and 6 are worth. I would not write it until a second wave exists.

Non-negotiable carry-over: the RULES must move into `SKILL.md` prose in the same commit — no self-review, approval is dated before the fan-in, the gate passes on the merged snapshot, a worker summary is never acceptance evidence. Those are the only load-bearing ideas in 27,663 lines, and they are four sentences. Keep `docs/evidence/waves/f83f-w1/` as committed bytes; it stays readable JSON forever, it just stops being re-derivable.
audits.risk_if_deleted:
Nothing an operator runs invokes any of it, so there is no runtime failure to name. `/sdlc-wave` — the actual delivered command — never mentions these six tools; `mise.toml`, `lefthook.yml` and `.github/workflows/validate.yml` contain zero references; `scripts/validate_bundle.py` has zero references; every sibling-tool "reference" is a docstring or a schema-name string constant. The only consumer in the entire repo is 7 lines of `skills/agentic-sdlc/SKILL.md` prose instructing an agent to run them.

Three specific, bounded failures:

1. BUILD-TIME, certain, ~10 lines of edits. `validate_bundle.py`'s broken-reference check fails until `SKILL.md:164-165, 170, 174, 199, 201, 263` and the one line in `references/readiness-composition.md` are edited in the same commit. Fix it in the deletion commit and `mise run check` stays green.

2. CAPABILITY, real but small. The repo loses its only mechanical answer to "was the fan-in approval recorded before the merge, and was the reviewer a different node than the implementer?" (`wave-verdict.py` conditions 4 and 5). This is the one genuinely load-bearing idea here and it deserves a rebuttal: AGENTS.md treats "only an authorized integrator executes an already authorized fan-in mutation" as a trust boundary, and condition 5 refusing an authorization recorded after the effect is a real control against an agent retroactively minting its own approval. But it is a control the controlled party may simply decline to invoke — the module says so itself ("nothing here can stop a dispatch"; a recorded budget "is bookkeeping the conductor must choose to obey") — and over the repo's entire history the conductor declined it every time but one. A check the audited party optionally runs on itself is discipline, not enforcement, so the preservation obligation is to keep the RULE where it is actually read, not the 12,209 lines that implement it optionally.

3. IRREVERSIBLE, trivial. `docs/evidence/waves/f83f-w1/projection.json` and `verdict.json` stop being re-derivable. They stay readable as committed bytes.

Now the risk in the other direction, which is measured rather than hypothetical. In its entire lifetime this subsystem has recorded ONE wave — `wave-f83f-w1`, on 2026-08-21, one day before this audit — and that wave delivered a 62-line bugfix (13 lines of production code, 49 of test) in commit 8958d6c. It produced 28 committed artifacts and 57 intermediate state files for it. The operator's own audit the same day states it plainly: "**no wave has ever been driven through them**"; the wave was then executed specifically to satisfy Slice 5's exit artifact, i.e. the wave was run to justify the machinery, not the machinery built to serve waves. `sdlc-observability-projection.py` — 1,928 lines with 3,657 lines of tests, the 4th-largest test file in the repository — produced no output even in that one wave; no document carrying its schema exists anywhere on disk or in git.

Meanwhile it is actively costing the operator. Seven seeds are open against it, and two quantify the damage: `agentic-sdlc-b284` records that `wave-journal.py`'s use of Linux-only `renameat2` was "the LARGEST macOS cluster: 172 of 554 ERROR/FAIL occurrences in CI run 32554149554", and `agentic-sdlc-e8a9` raises that to ~238 and notes it "poisoned every fixture built on journal init ... across four suites" by escalating a clean exit-3 refusal to exit 4 effect-unknown. So this subsystem, used once, on Linux, is responsible for roughly a third to nearly half of the macOS CI failure surface, and the portable Darwin primitive it needed was already sitting in `install_research_os.py:2028` unused. Six more of its nineteen closed seeds are "close the residuals left by the adversarial review" of these same tools: it generates its own maintenance work.

Against the stated vision — "mise config + opencodex + a few scripts + a whole lotta skills + a few hooks, wrapped in a plugin + cli-tool combo" — 27,663 lines of self-enforced JSON protocol is not a few scripts, is not a skill, and has no slot in ADR-0021's topology (mise → versioned release → one `ccodex` CLI → per-host install): it is not installed machinery, not a gate leaf, and not a CLI verb. Deleting it is lower-risk than keeping it.

One adjacency for the conductor, not my subsystem to claim: `drift-classifier.py` consumes a `wave-plan@1` document that only `wave-plan-compiler.py` produces, so deleting this orphans its input producer — a further 2,915 lines (1,515 + 1,400 tests), with `auto-envelope.py` (2,564 + 2,678) one hop behind it, since it consumes the drift classification.

audits.what_it_does: Four tools implementing ADR-0022's assess-plan-approve-apply-readback lifecycle for one target repository. `repository-classifier.py` answers greenfield / brownfield / refuse-and-ask by hand-parsing the Git object store — loose refs, `packed-refs`, raw zlib commit and tree objects, entry modes — with no subprocess, so it can conclude "provably empty" without trusting git. `activation-planner.py` is a general-purpose transactional single-file writer: `plan --target --manifest --entry` renders one output through `instruction-generator.py`, binds the target's statx mount IDs and descriptor-relative parent chain, observes Git cleanliness, and emits a digest-sealed plan; `apply --plan --manifest --grant` consumes that digest plus a single-use same-user grant and writes the file through a private transaction directory with stage / backup / discard payloads, a numbered progress journal, and commit, receipt, rollback and audit records living in a machine-local state plane (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/ccodex/activation/<sha256 of target>`) reachable through per-checkout plane pointers; `status` and `recover inspect|finish|rollback` read and finish or reverse an interrupted one. `planning-snapshot.py` captures and seals the observed-state half of a planning artifact chain, and `repository-contract.py` reads a ten-field all-strings `.agentic-sdlc/repo.toml`. The single deliverable of all of it is one markdown file: a marker-delimited `<!-- agentic-sdlc:start -->` block spliced into `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`. `plan` produces exactly one entry or zero, and the desired mode is hardcoded `0o644`.
audits.replacement:
Four concrete pieces, ~220 lines total, three of which already exist.

1. KEEP `instruction-generator.py` (209 lines, pure, already renders the block and already detects/locates an existing marked block via `locate_marked_block`). Add an `apply` verb, ~45 lines: `os.open(path, O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW)`, splice the block, print a unified diff, require `--yes`, write temp-plus-rename in the same directory. Approve and write in one invocation. That deletes the plan document, the grant, the eight schema versions, the 922 lines (21% of the planner) that re-validate documents the same process wrote seconds earlier, the state plane, the plane pointers, the progress journal, and all three `recover` verbs — because every one of them exists only to bridge a gap between two invocations that no longer exist.

2. REPLACE the classifier with ~25 lines: `git ls-files -z -- AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md mise.toml lefthook.yml .seeds docs/adr .github .gitlab-ci.yml .agentic-sdlc` plus `test -e` on the same paths in the working tree. Anything occupied → brownfield, name it. Nothing occupied AND `git rev-list --count HEAD` ≤ 1 AND clean `git status --porcelain` → propose greenfield, still ask. Anything else → refuse-and-ask. # Bun CLI spike: verdict

**The premise is wrong on its most important claim.** I reproduced mechanism L and it is not a bash-interpreter property. A compiled binary is affected identically. Recommendation: **do not do the rewrite as framed.**

## What I built

`/tmp/bun-cli-spike/src/` — 590 lines, ports the real security core of `scripts/opencodex-claude.sh`:

| file | lines | ports |
|---|---|---|
| `settings.ts` | 131 | `settings_bypass_classification()` (the `jq -ers` program), all 6 model slots, 4 switches, loopback + cloud-id regexes |
| `resolve.ts` | 66 | the `jq()` resolver + ADR-0020 rules |
| `argv.ts` | 89 | `assert_forwarded_settings_are_effective()` + an argv diagnostic bash cannot have |
| `refuse.ts` | 67 | `refuse()`, `settings_argument_refusal()`, exit contract |
| `env.ts` | 93 | allowlist + `Bun.spawn` |
| `cli.ts` | 140 | entrypoint |
| `test/spike.test.ts` | 219 | 24 tests |

## 1. Compile, size, startup

```
[15ms]  bundle  6 modules
[142ms] compile  dist/spike
82547912 bytes  (79M)
```
`--minify` saves 4 KB; `--bytecode` **adds** 57 KB. `strip` saves 48 KB (see below — it also destroys the binary).

```
compiled binary        (spike --version)       min   21.55 ms   mean   24.39 ms   (n=20)
bun interpreting TS   (bun run src/cli.ts)     min   22.82 ms   mean   24.36 ms   (n=20)
bash: real 2025-line launcher --help           min    7.75 ms   mean    8.69 ms   (n=20)
bash: /bin/true floor (interpreter only)       min    1.72 ms   mean    1.94 ms   (n=20)
```

**The binary is 2.8x slower to start than the 2,025-line bash script.** Bash parses 2,025 lines in 8.7 ms; `--compile` buys nothing over `bun run`.

That reverses on the path that matters, because `jq_available()` is deliberately uncached and the pinned route is `mise -C "$root" exec -- jq` at **22.34 ms per spawn**:

```
bash floor: 6 pinned mise-jq spawns (3 docs)       min  116.51 ms   mean  130.39 ms
compiled binary: same 3 documents in-process       min   21.75 ms   mean   24.48 ms
```

**5.3x faster on the real settings gate.** No runtime extraction: 1 write-open total, a failed `trace_marker` probe. Deterministic for a fixed `--outfile` (the filename is an input to the hash).

## 2. Cross-compilation — 12 targets from this one Linux x64 host

OK: `linux-x64`, `linux-x64-baseline`, `linux-arm64`, `linux-x64-musl`, `linux-arm64-musl`, `darwin-arm64`, `darwin-x64`, `darwin-x64-baseline`, `windows-x64`, `windows-arm64`, `freebsd-x64`, `android-arm64` (all verified genuine via `file`, not fallbacks).

```
bun-linux-armv7              FAIL: error: Unsupported target "armv7" in "bun-linux-armv7"
bun-linux-riscv64            FAIL: error: Unsupported target "riscv64" in "bun-linux-riscv64"
bun-linux-x86                FAIL: error: Unsupported target "x86" in "bun-linux-x86"
bun-windows-x86              FAIL: error: Unsupported target "x86" in "bun-windows-x86"
bun-openbsd-x64              FAIL: error: Unsupported target "openbsd" in "bun-openbsd-x64"
```

No 32-bit anything, **no armv7** — this tree lives under `custom-pi-setup`, and 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS is untargetable. musl needs `libc.musl` + `libstdc++` and does **not** run on a glibc host, so it's a separate artifact.

The Windows binary cross-built here **runs as a real Windows process** (verified via WSL interop): `"platform": "win32"`.

## 3. The four defects

**(a) Pinned resolution — PASS, structurally.** The positive control is the finding:
```json
{ "binding": "jq", "route": "unadmitted",
  "runnable": false,
  "pathWouldHaveResolvedJqTo": "/usr/bin/jq" }
```
PATH *would* have found it; the route refused at exit 3. A hostile `jq` echoing `clean`, placed first on PATH, cannot suppress a refusal.

**(b) JSON without jq — PASS, definitively.** A full classify is **exactly 1 `execve`** (the binary itself) and works with `PATH=/nonexistent`. This retires jq, `jq_available()`'s uncached re-probing, the `unreadable: the admitted jq route could not be run` degradation path, and the ERE-vs-Oniguruma agreement requirement (two engines → one `RegExp`). The measured leading-space bypass is caught:
```
REFUSED: ... sets ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL to ` global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5[1m]` ...
exit=3
```

**(c) Windows argv — FAILED. The premise is wrong.**

The repo's `run-git-bash.ps1` does not pass argv; it builds a shell **string** and runs `bash -lc`. Chasing that, I reproduced the defect under **Windows PowerShell 5.1.22621.6133** (`PSNativeCommandArgumentPassing: (unset / not supported on this PS)`):

```
value PS holds: <<{"ultracode":true}>> len=18

=== A. PS 5.1 -> NATIVE BUN BINARY, direct argv (no wrapper, no -lc) ===
  [1] len=16 <<{ultracode:true}>>          <-- QUOTES STRIPPED
=== B. PS 5.1 -> Git Bash -lc STRING -> bash script (the repo wrapper today) ===
  [0] len=16 <<{ultracode:true}>>          <-- identical corruption
=== C. PS 5.1 -> Git Bash, argv form ===
  [1] len=14 <<ultracode:true>>            <-- worse
```

The value isn't lost, it's **corrupted into invalid JSON** — which then classifies as "not a valid JSON object", a refusal blaming the operator. That fully explains 34 CI failures. It is a PowerShell 5.1 CreateProcess marshalling defect that hits **every** native executable, compiled Bun binary included. There is no interpreter to remove.

Worse: going native *enters* an MSYS2 layer the `.sh` file is immune to.
```
Git Bash -> NATIVE binary:   /usr/bin:/bin (13) -> C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin;C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin (57)
                             /             (1)  -> C:/Program Files/Git/ (21)
Git Bash -> MSYS2 bash:      /usr/bin:/bin (13) -> /usr/bin:/bin (13)   [verbatim]
MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*':     verbatim for the native binary too
```

Remedies, **all language-independent** — a one-line fix to `Quote-Bash`, not a 3,060-line rewrite:
```
R1 file path         : 35 chars intact
R2 base64            : 24 chars intact
R3 single-quoted JSON: 18 intact   (confirms it is specifically the double quote)
R4 \" escaping       : 18 intact, arrives as correct {"ultracode":true}
```
What the binary genuinely adds is **observability**: it printed the argv it received. The forensics pass could not recover that.

**(d) Refuse by name — PASS.** `0` clean, `3` refused, `2` usage/unknown verb, `1` unrunnable bound executable, `3` bare-name binding.

Bonus: mechanism L's two causes are now distinguishable from a CI log alone — `--settings` alone reports `argv received: 1 argument(s)` / "no value followed it"; `--settings ''` reports `argv[1] len=0 <<EMPTY STRING>>` / "present but empty".

## 4. Environment allowlist

The child's own `/usr/bin/env` output, with the parent exporting three secrets:
```
"childStdout": ["HOME=...","LANG=C.UTF-8","PATH=/usr/bin:/bin","SPIKE_INJECTED=yes","TERM=...","USER=..."]
"deniedNames": ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY","AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY","CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK"]
```
PATH is constructed, not inherited. No shell, so `$(touch /tmp/pwned-by-spike); rm -rf /; \`id\`` passes verbatim and the file is not created.

## 5. Tests

`bun test` — zero config, zero dependencies:
```
24 pass / 0 fail / 83 expect() calls / [26.00ms]
```
Per this repo's own `verify-tests-by-mutation-not-by-reading` lesson, I mutation-verified rather than read:
```
M1 drop whitespace trim                       23 pass 1 fail
M2 model-slot shape check disabled            21 pass 3 fail
M3 console-key prefix flipped to sk-ant-oat   23 pass 1 fail
M4 foreign base-URL check disabled            23 pass 1 fail
M5 bare-name binding admitted (6f9d restored) 22 pass 2 fail
M6 -- terminator ignored                      23 pass 1 fail
M7 missing/empty messages made identical      23 pass 1 fail
```
Sources restored clean (`diff` verified). Compare `mise run check`: 3,308 tests / 913 s.

## 6. Honest costs

**Bun is not a runtime dependency** — the binary runs with bun off PATH (`isCompiledBinary: true`), no extraction. It *is* a build dependency.

**Still an interpreter, just a universal one:** `/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`. glibc floor is **2.17** — *below* the repo's existing 2.28 requirement, so not a new constraint. The shebang class (seed 5cbd) *is* genuinely eliminated: `7f454c46`, no `#!`.

**Size:** 5-platform release = **388,489,426 bytes (370 MiB)**; `gzip -9` linux-x64 = 36,604,288 (35 MB). The bash CLI is ~120 KB. ~3,000x.

**Unpinned supply chain — the biggest cost.** `--compile --target` fetched 10 runtimes (61–85 MB each, cache now 1.9 GB), and:
```
=== is any digest recorded for these in the project? ===
  NOTHING in bun.lock or package.json pins a compile-target runtime
```
For a repo whose validator "pins the supply chain by digest," this introduces a network-fetched, unpinned blob that becomes **>99.99% of the bytes operators execute**.

**macOS signing — a real release step, and an asymmetry:**
```
darwin-arm64: CodeDirectory flags=0x20002 adhoc=YES identifier='a.out'  -> AD-HOC, no CMS
darwin-x64  : CodeDirectory flags=0x10000 adhoc=no  identifier='bun'   -> REAL CMS, 8975 bytes
```
Both `codeLimit`s fully cover the payload. But neither is signed under an identity this project controls — arm64 is ad-hoc (runs locally; a *downloaded* copy gets quarantined), x64 carries **Oven's** `bun` identity. A release needs its own Developer ID + `notarytool` step. Confirming x64's CMS validity needs a macOS runner.

**`strip` silently destroys the binary — and passes a smoke test:**
```
=== unstripped ===        0.0.1-spike
=== STRIPPED, same argv === 1.4.0
--- selftest on stripped ---  error: Script not found "selftest"   EXIT=1
--- does the stripped one still refuse? --- error: Script not found "check-settings"  EXIT=1
```
`strip` is in half the world's release Makefiles. A stripped binary answers `--version` with **exit 0 and a plausible version**, then fails every real verb — and a refusal exits 1 instead of 3. That is precisely the seed-5cbd shape: reports success, fails at every exec.

**`--bytecode` forbids top-level await:** `error: "await" can only be used inside an "async" function`. The fast-startup flag and the idiomatic entrypoint are mutually exclusive.

**The line-count saving is ~400, not 3,060:**
```
opencodex-claude.sh    2025 lines  1190 code   835 comment/blank
spike src/              590 lines   414 code
```
835 of 2,025 bash lines are **comments encoding measured forensics** ("MEASURED 2026-08-11 against Claude Code 2.1.227…"). Those are the most valuable bytes in the file, and a rewrite must port them verbatim, not delete them.

## Recommendation

**Don't rewrite. Fix the four defects where they actually live.**

Three of the four cited defects were already fixed in bash. The fourth — the only open one, and the one that motivated the question — is **not a bash defect at all**. It is PowerShell 5.1 argument marshalling, and I measured the compiled binary suffering it identically. The fix is `\"`-escaping or a temp-file path in `run-git-bash.ps1`: hours, one file, testable today. Rewriting 3,060 lines would have shipped a binary with the *same* bug plus a 370 MiB unpinned artifact, an unowned macOS signature, and a `strip` landmine that passes smoke tests.

Bun's real win here isn't compilation — it's **deleting jq**: 1 execve instead of 6 spawns, 130 ms → 24 ms, and the retirement of ADR-0020's entire resolution problem plus the two-regex-engine agreement requirement. That is worth harvesting on its own.

**Strongest counterargument, which I take seriously:** the `strip`/PowerShell/MSYS2 findings all cut the *other* way on evidence quality. Every bash defect on the list took real production failures or CI forensics to find, and one is still marked "mechanism unknown" — because bash's argv is unrecoverable. In this spike I diagnosed that unknown mechanism to an exact PowerShell version in about ten minutes, precisely because a program can print what it received. If the repo keeps paying multi-day forensics bills on unobservable shell boundaries, "we can always instrument it" is worth more than 370 MiB. The disciplined version of that argument is not a rewrite: port the **settings classifier** — the highest-blast-radius, most-forensics-heavy, jq-dependent surface — to a Bun binary invoked *by* the existing bash launcher, keep the shell for orchestration, and pin the target runtime by digest before anything ships. That harvests the 5.3x and the observability while risking one function instead of a whole CLI.

# HALF ONE — Safety-preservation rebuttal

I went looking for the failure each subsystem was built to prevent before agreeing to kill it. Sources: `docs/adr/0019–0025`, `docs/research/2026-08-22-ci-red-forensics.md`, commits `c5ea877`, `374eec6`, `d456f62`, and the 36 open seeds in `.seeds/issues.jsonl`.

## 1. Install/ownership lifecycle (shrink-hard) — rebuttal FAILS; shrink stands, with one doctrine cost named

The witness layer's origin story is in its own commit: `374eec6` ("settle birth-timestamp witnesses so a replaced tree is never removed") cites CI run 32554149554, and the forensics addendum measured the runner: **"identical `(inode, btime)` pair in 20 of 20 trials"** — on the reference CI platform the `stat-v2` witness "carries no discriminating information at all." So the strongest evidence about this control is that it fails open exactly where it is tested, fails closed (refusing installs entirely) on NFS/FUSE/musl hosts, and its settlement machinery exists to appease a probe the repo wrote about its own scheme. The audit's substitution (the `install_operator_tools.py` shape, already shipping and tested) is a real design in this tree, not a sketch.

What the rebuttal DOES establish: deleting the witness honestly weakens AGENTS.md's promise that "foreign, retargeted, and modified entries are preserved" from *physical identity* to *byte identity*. A byte-identical operator re-copy will now be removed by uninstall. The harm is bounded — the bytes removed are the bundle's own — but the doctrine prose in AGENTS.md must be weakened in the same commit, or it becomes the exact "prose that asserts a command result" rot the operator's memory warns about. Also verified: `scripts/ccodex_sdlc_install.py:1782` loads this module as a sibling and uses `bundle.Config`, `transactional_*`, `installer_lock`, `entry_matches_record` — the surviving ~1,530-line core must keep those names or update that consumer in the same change.

## 2. Acquisition engine (shrink-hard) — the conductor's exploit is evidence FOR the shrink, and here is why

The exploit is already fixed, and the fix is the argument. `c5ea877` (agentic-sdlc-4c49): the engine's `_identity` tuple "carries two timestamp terms, and they are the only terms that witness a same-length in-place write to a held inode… filesystem granularity was the only thing standing between the attacker and an accepted verdict." What closed it: `_copy_fd_at` now "digests exactly the bytes it writes and refuses `archive-mutated` unless they equal the plan-admitted `archive_sha256`" — **133 production lines, zero extra I/O**. The 12,242-line witness/journal/grant scaffold was defeated by clock granularity; the small content-digest check is the control that held, and it is "strictly stronger than a post-copy re-read."

So the exploit is evidence that *whatever publishes bytes must hash the bytes it publishes against an admitted digest* — a ~40-line obligation — not evidence for the engine. Three more facts seal it: (a) ADR-0021's accepted decision is "exact release artifacts resolved by mise… because mise already owns version selection" — the engine is a parallel reimplementation of the acquirer the ADR already assigned to mise, whose lockfile checksums are the same control; (b) the engine disclaims its own adversary in writing (same-UID racer out of scope, `grant.approval_authenticated: false`) yet carries three OPEN trust-boundary seeds against that adversary (`c1f5`, `ba1a`, `db15`) — it generates a defect stream against a threat it has declared unsupported; (c) `ccodex_sdlc_install.py` re-derives the receipt seal and re-verifies every copied entry against the manifest anyway, so extraction-time proof is proven again at activation. **Non-negotiable carry-over:** the receipt shim must itself re-hash the mise-resolved root against `manifest.json` before sealing — that is where the 4c49 lesson lands.

## 3. Wave/journal/verdict stack (delete) — the rebuttal lands ONE real blow: this deletion is an ADR reversal, and it must be executed as one

The strongest defense of this stack is not in its code, it is in `docs/adr/0025` (accepted, operator-decided): "Compile immutable typed planning generations and diff them explicitly — chosen because every execution and continuation can bind to one reviewed generation… drift can be hidden as 'continuation' and auto mode can broaden itself without a new approval." And ADR-0024 decision 6 requires completion evidence. Deleting the stack without touching those records leaves two accepted ADRs describing machinery that does not exist — exactly the silent rot the memory files warn about. Four open slice-5 seeds (`8749`, `4a07`, `a2f8`, `3b5e`) are actively building on this stack; deleting it strands them undispositioned. And the cascade is bigger than the audit's scope: `drift-classifier.py` + `auto-envelope.py` (~10.5k more lines) implement ADR-0025 decisions 4–5 and go with it.

But on the merits the deletion survives the rebuttal. The stack's genuinely load-bearing control — condition 5, approval recorded before the effect, which is ADR-0019's fresh-authorization doctrine — is not enforcement in either form: the JSON chain is "detection, not prevention," writable by the same-UID conductor it audits, and the module concedes "nothing here can stop a dispatch." A hand-written dated blockquote next to a committer date has the same evidentiary strength against the same forger. Measured against that: one wave ever recorded (run to satisfy its own exit artifact), zero consumers in `mise.toml`/`lefthook.yml`/CI (re-verified this session — grep is empty), and per seeds `b284`/`e8a9` its Linux-only `renameat2` is responsible for ~238 of the macOS CI failures. **Delete, as a package:** supersede ADR-0025 / amend ADR-0024, move the four rules into `SKILL.md` prose, re-disposition the slice-5 seeds, and decide the drift-classifier/auto-envelope cascade in the same ADR rather than leaving it orphaned.

## 4. Activation planner (delete) — same shape: defensible only with ADR-0022 amended

ADR-0022 rejected "keep activation as a conversational runbook… because a prose plan cannot be replayed, digest-approved, transactionally applied, or independently read back." The audit's replacement is not the rejected option — it is deterministic, diff-approved, `O_NOFOLLOW`, temp-plus-rename, in ONE invocation, which removes the two-invocation TOCTOU window the plan digest exists to close. The dropped piece is ADR-0022 decision 3's machine-local receipt — and the measured record is that no receipt has ever had a reader: 70 orphan records, all keyed to deleted `/tmp` fixtures; the tool never activated the repository that ships it.
